analysis:
Compared supplied BASE/HEAD publication and preload source, Serve patch, and file metadata against the indexed threat model and detailed T-041. No independently supported regression is established in this scope. PrefetchPublication.swift:48 adds advertisement-occurrence tracking before hashing and possible refusal; :261-265 expands Autopilot inventory through joinsAutopilotSetWhenVerified. Existing nonempty-hash, runtime/adapter eligibility, failed-self-test, retirement, revision, memory-floor and announcement rollback checks remain. These are relevant to A-004, T-007/T-012/T-027 and availability across TB-002/TB-007; model hashes do not establish correct computation or serving authorization (T-056).
Preload.swift:30 replaces autopilotAllowsModel with autopilotServesModel; residency-command refusal, runtime eligibility, shutdown/drain checks and task-ID-fenced completion (:119-135) remain. Removing private visibility from two helpers is module-internal, not itself a remote interface. Serve.swift:289 starts candidate verification; :477-480 shuts down a download coordinator and cancels verification. No supplied change directly alters prompt encryption, credential custody, App Attest grants, billing, cache scoping or T-041 disk protections.
Integration must inspect the new helper implementations and callers: whether joinsAutopilotSetWhenVerified enforces saved consent and verified catalog identity; whether autopilotServesModel preserves selection and retirement restrictions; whether occurrence tracking at publication :48 invalidates pending work even when publication fails; and whether startup verification/downloads have bounded resource use and cannot publish after shutdown. Trace these against revision drains, inventory rollback and reconnect registration, and ensure expanded inventory does not substitute for T-052/T-053 authorization. These contracts are outside the supplied evidence, not observed missing controls; their uncertainty prevents a security conclusion on the combined PR.
